title: Your Small Business Loan Just Got a Longer Safety Net
description: The government has extended a special fund that helps small businesses get loans. This fund, called the Credit Guarantee Fund, now covers loans under the Prad.

faq.q: Who manages the Credit Guarantee Fund?
faq.a: The Credit Guarantee Fund is typically managed by a trust or institution set up by the government, such as the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) for Mudra loans.

faq.q: Are all types of businesses covered under these schemes?
faq.a: PMMY covers non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises. Stand Up India focuses on greenfield enterprises (new ventures) by women and SC/ST entrepreneurs in manufacturing, services, or trading sectors.

faq.q: What happens if a borrower misuses the loan?
faq.a: Banks conduct due diligence before sanctioning loans. Misuse of funds can lead to legal action and the borrower still remains liable for repayment, even if the bank recovers some amount from the guarantee fund.

faq.q: Does the loan interest rate change because of the guarantee?
faq.a: The interest rates are set by the lending institutions as per RBI guidelines, but the reduced risk for banks due to the guarantee can sometimes lead to more favourable terms for borrowers compared to unsecured loans without such a guarantee.

fact_check.summary: The article accurately reports on the extension of the Credit Guarantee Fund for PMMY and Stand Up India schemes, including key dates, loan limits, and the managing authority. It provides a reliable overview of the schemes' mechanics and benefits.

corrections.note: Corrected the maximum loan limit for Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) to include the 'Tarun Plus' category and clarified the managing entity for the Credit Guarantee Fund for Mudra loans.

edits.why: The Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) is managed by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC) and specifically covers Mudra loans.
